data.narrative:
Hyperscale Power is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Rothmund (PhD ETH Zurich, ex-ABB) and Sami Pettersson (ex-ABB), having raised €5M to date. The target sector comprises a peer universe of 1 public company (LNZA) and 8 private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method is applicable here, using the €5M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding €12M. A peer-median approach is not applicable; while 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, filtering for stage-comparable, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier companies yields fewer than 3 datapoints, making median benchmarking unreliable and potentially misleading at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of €11M (low) to €14M (high), with a midpoint of €12M. This range reflects a single methodological input, creating material uncertainty around the valuation. Key uncertainties include the lack of narrow-set peer comparables, which limits confidence in stage-progression multipliers, and the early-stage nature of the company, where revenue or unit economics data are likely unavailable for independent validation. Any refinement would require either identification of additional stage-proximate peers or disclosure of revenue, burn rate, or technology milestones.
